ov: Small bony fish, 47 species, named for their horse-like head and neck. They swim upright, have bony armour instead of scales and a curled tail for gripping, and the male carries the eggs in a pouch until the young are born.

why.et: Dried seahorses are widely used in traditional Chinese medicine, despite no clinical evidence that they work.
why.p: Kept by aquarium hobbyists, though wild-caught seahorses tend to do poorly in home tanks.

df: Small shrimps and other tiny prey.
fx: A female can deposit up to 1,500 eggs in the male’s pouch, and he carries them for 9–45 days.
The dwarf seahorse is the slowest-moving fish in the world, with a top speed of about 1.5 m an hour.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact (the male gets pregnant) is confirmed. PAGE ADDITIONS 2026-11-02 (ov, fx), from the cached Wikipedia text. The article gives no weight, and only habitats (seas, estuaries, lagoons), not a range.
